cohort: The study included 110 pregnant women with non-cephalic fetal presentations who were offered an ECV procedure at term between October 2023 and November 2024.
finding: External cephalic version, particularly with regional anesthesia, was found to be a feasible and effective strategy for reducing cesarean section rates, with 63.9% of attempts being successful and regional anesthesia significantly reducing procedural pain.
mod_finding: ECV implementation resulted in a 2.12% reduction in the overall cesarean section rate at the institution, with successful ECV attempts leading to vaginal deliveries.
